notes.title: SAND | May Development Update
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/5207e26c16a61750d418845d76e84781dea1f2a9.png

Servus Scavengers!

With the announcement that SAND is coming to consoles earlier this week at the tinyBuild Connect, we thought it was only fair we give some updates to our PC players on what's going on at the Hologryph HQ and how development is coming along!

So today, we asked Maksym, the head of studio at Hologryph what he and the team are doing and how SAND is shaping up. Let's take a look at what he had to say...

What are the current focuses for the development team at this stage?

Currently, the team is focusing on three main areas:

[olist]
 Throughout April and May, we created many prototypes and searched for a final gameplay form that would address the issues we identified with your help during the last playtest. In the coming months, we’ll be finalizing the elements that passed internal testing and building balance around the new set of features.
 Optimization and bug fixing.
 Porting the game to PS5 and Xbox Series (together with support from an external studio). The external studio is handling most of the work. Our involvement is limited to providing guidance on project structure, and occasionally doing tasks that are significantly faster for us to complete. This does not affect the release timeline for the PC version.
[/olist]
Do you have any new/unannounced content or features in the works?

We have a number of new features currently in development. Not all of them will pass internal testing, so I can’t talk about all of them just yet.

What you can expect in the playtest:

[olist]
 Weapon Modifications – Different weapons will have variations that can be crafted or found during gameplay.
 Turret Deployment – You'll be able to place and remove turrets during an expedition, which ties in with the next point. 
 Turret Conditions – Turrets will come in various states, ranging from “rusty” to “fresh off the shelf.” The condition affects certain turret characteristics, such as rotation speed and reload time.
[/olist]
How are optimizations coming along/what has been done?

As part of the console porting process, we’re currently optimizing the game for launch on Xbox Series S, which will also result in stable fps on many PCs with similar performance levels.

At this stage, the optimization process has touched nearly every aspect of the game:

 How the terrain is generated, stored in memory, and unloaded
 Trampler compartment models, including the number and quality of their LODs
 Visual effects like reactor smoke or explosions from destroyed Trampler units
 Character animation system
 Loot generation system for islands and points of interest
 Network data format for certain systems
 And some more extremely cool stuff we're not ready to share just yet, but we'll show you in the near future...

And of course, the work is still ongoing...

What has changed lately from previous playtests?


 New islands and partially reworked old ones
 New types of firearms + a grenade
 Crafting stations on certain islands, and a crafting compartment for the Trampler. Plus a wide variety of crafting resources scattered across the map
 Ability to swap out cannons during an expedition
 Many cannon variations, including several [REDACTED]-grade cannons
 New compartments
 A progression system that gradually unlocks access to more advanced compartments
 An orbital station shop where you can sell your findings and buy basic expedition supplies
 A loot distribution system after each expedition to ensure everyone gets what they need
 You can name your Trampler now
 Boost rods that temporarily accelerate the Trampler, helping you escape pursuit—or close the gap on enemies
 [REDACTED]—diverse, powerful, and mysterious

Finally, can we expect another playtest before launch?

That’s the plan! We hope to have a playtest this summer to show off everything we’ve been working on the last few months, but you’ll have to wait a little longer for some more firm details on that. 

You can sign up for any closed or open playtests on the Steam page right now though, and you’ll be notified directly via Steam when they go live.

[hr][/hr]

notes.title: SAND | April Development Update - Q&A Edition
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/410404ebd995c39d27c3d52411e1975204edc808.jpg

Hello folks!

For this months development update, we've collected all of your most pressing questions about SAND and stuck them in front of the wonderful development team at Hologryph for some answers.

So let's jump into your questions and see what the devs had to say...

Release Date & Pricing

“When is the game coming out?”

 We haven’t set a new release date for SAND yet, as our focus is on getting the game right, not just getting it out. Once we’re happy with the additional work these extra few months of development have afforded us and we’re confident SAND will meet the expectations of our players, a release date will be finalized and we’ll announce it, so stay tuned!

“How much will the game cost?”

We haven’t announced the price yet, but our goal is to make the game accessible to as many players as possible and to foster a strong online community. This will be reflected in the price, which we’ll share a little closer to release.

“Will there be another playtest?”

Playtests have been an incredibly important part of SANDs development to date, and of course we'll need to confer with our community to make sure everything is up to scratch before our eventual launch, so it's a safe bet.

Consoles & Platforms

“Will the game be available on consoles?”

 Our current focus is on the PC version, but we’re definitely interested in bringing SAND to consoles in the future.

“Will it run on midrange gaming laptops?”

We’re hard at work optimizing the game to work across a broad variety of setups and configurations and should have our updated system specs available in the near future.

“Will it support Linux (e.g. Proton/Debian)?”

 We’re not currently working towards Linux support, but should we see enough demand from our community in the future it’s something we’re open to exploring.

Servers & Regions

“Will there be more server regions available upon launch than there were during the playtests”

We’re working on regional server support and hope to have as many regions available on launch as feasibly possible. Stay tuned for updates.

“Can I choose my server region?”

Yes, you can select from the available regions. However, your progress won't transfer between regions for now.

Trampler Customization & Features

“Will there be stylized or more trampler skins?”

 We’re exploring more visual customization options and already have some cool ideas in the pipeline.

“Will there be weaponized or ramming builds?”

Yes, a ramming compartment will be available at launch and we might even share some early looks at that very soon...

“Can I test my trampler before entering a match?”

Not currently. We may add an option to view your Trampler more closely in the editor, but full test-driving won’t be possible at launch. We’re keeping the idea in mind for the future however…

Weapons & Combat Systems

“Will there be more weapons and gun mods?”

Yes! More weapons are being added, and you can customize them at a workbench, either on your Trampler (if equipped with a crafting compartment) or at workbenches found on islands.

“Will there be melee or unique weapons like sandworms, grappling hooks, or mine layers?”

These types of unique weapons are under consideration, we’ll share more details as development progresses. Knuckle dusters are currently being tested, so we’ll have at least one melee type weapon at launch.

Progression & Gameplay Loops

“What will long-term progression look like?”

We’re working on a system where you’ll build relationships with factions on the space station to unlock advanced compartments. To do that, you’ll need to explore the surface and collect valuable resources. This is another thing we’re hoping to share some more details about very soon!

“Will there be skill trees, crafting, or side quests?”

 Crafting: yes.
 Skill tree: no, but there is a tech tree.
 Side quests: not at launch but it’s something we’ve discussed extensively and would like to explore.

“Will there be more to do on expeditions (missions, NPCs, factions)?”

We’re working to better integrate strategic and tactical goals. Strategically, your aim is to upgrade your Trampler. Tactically, it’s about surviving, finding resources, and making smart choices. Expect diverse surface locations like refineries, abandoned factories, or military outposts, and more to be added in the future each with different challenges and rewards.

PvE / PvP Balance

“Will solo play be viable?”

 Yes, SAND is designed to be enjoyable whether you play solo or with friends.

“Will there be non-combat progression?”

Absolutely. A significant amount of the tech tree can be advanced through non-combat activities.

“What about griefing or overly competitive PvP players?”

We’re aware of these concerns and working to balance the experience to support a wide range of playstyles and will do everything we can to combat griefers.

Building & Systems

“Will you continue developing the Trampler editor?”

For now, development on the Trampler editor has paused as we focus on other features. But let us know what additions you’d like to see!

“Can I build bases in the world, not just on Trampler?”

Your Trampler is your mobile base. You won’t be able to build permanent structures on the surface, only explore and return to the space station.

“Will there be tutorials?”

Yes, basic tutorials will be available via F1 on each screen. More advanced tutorials will come later.

World & Exploration

“How big is the map?”

We’re currently testing a 12x12 km map internally.

“Will there be different biomes (snow zones, coral graveyards)?”

Yes, additional biomes are planned for future updates.

“Will there be sandstorms or other dynamic events?”

We’re actively designing new events. Two are in concept right now, but we’re not ready to reveal them yet (but we can say that you won’t be disappointed…).

Other

“Will there be proximity chat?”

There certainly will! We’re planning mid-range proximity chat so nearby Trampler crews can communicate.

“Will tramplers get 45° angled cannons?”

It’s on our to-do list!

“Can we drink the crates of booze we find?”
Nope! It’s so rare and valuable that it’s basically undrinkable. Your throat won’t even let you try!

“Will there be tournaments or ranked modes?”

Not at launch.

“Can I play with friends but avoid PvP?”

Technically yes, if you avoid every smoke pillar you see. But SAND isn’t a PvE-focused game, so it’ll be tough but not impossible.

“Why can’t I buy ammo in space before a drop?”

We’re finishing up the orbital shop! Soon, you’ll be able to buy basic items, weapons, and ammo before expeditions.

“Can we control drones or build mini-vehicles?”

No, that won’t be a feature, as cool as it sounds!.

“Will you release the game’s soundtrack?”

If there’s enough demand, we’d certainly be open to the possibility. 

“Will there be whimsical decorations like ‘date night’ tables?”

We’d love to add more fun and quirky items like that, but performance optimization comes first.
“Can I squish players with my trampler?”

We tested this, but friendly trampler deaths were so frequent it broke the game. It’s on hold while we figure out a better way to implement it.

[hr][/hr]

Thank you to everyone who submitted questions, and if you have any questions on topics we didn't cover in the Q&A, feel free to drop them in the replies and we'll try and get them answered for you!

notes.title: SAND: An update on the Early Access release date
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/0c2e397bbf8eb665f82b64e161639b34b206c327.jpg

Hi All,

We wanted to provide an update on SAND and share that we have decided to delay the Early Access release.

With the initially planned Early Access release approaching, we’ve been working hard to ensure that SAND would meet the expectations of our awesome community and is able to deliver the experience we have envisioned for our players without any compromises.

During this time it’s become clear that in order to meet those goals, additional work is needed, so today we’ve made the tough decision to push SAND back to a later date.

As we work towards that date, we will be focusing heavily on these areas:

 Expanding and improving the core gameplay
 Further focusing on significant optimization and performance improvements

We understand that this is disappointing news, but it is not a decision we have made lightly, and we’re confident that it’s essential for us to ensure the best possible experience for you all when SAND enters Early Access later this year.

If you have any questions about this delay, the development of the game or anything else you’d like answered about SAND, feel free to leave your questions below and we’ll do our best to get them addressed in an upcoming development update.

We appreciate your patience and understanding here, stay tuned for the next development update where we’ll share some more details about what we’re working on and when you can expect to see SAND enter Early Access.

Hologryph / tinyBuild Games

notes.title: SAND | March Development Update
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/96e9beb9f368555f60171d527d874b27ccf3540f.jpg
Hello Scavengers!

With the Closed and Open Playtests and announcement of SAND launching into Early Access on April 3rd, February was a pretty crazy month for all of us here at tinyBuild and Hologryph and there's no signs of slowing down any time soon!

As the Early Access launch approaches, and with all the feedback, suggestions and reports from the recent beta still fresh in everyones minds, we wanted to give you all an update on what we're working on behind the scenes and what to expect from SAND when you all arrive back on Sophie in April.

So let's jump into it...

Optimization:

While we made a lot of major improvements in this field between the Steam Next Fest demo last year and the recent open playtest, we still saw a lot of reports of performance issues and general disappointment at the current levels of optimization, but rest assured we hear you and we are doing everything we can to address these complaints ahead of the launch into Early Access.

Here are some of the key areas we're working on right now

Inventory System Overhaul: 

We're reworking how inventory functions to reduce the number of client-server requests, which should help with responsiveness and performance.

Occlusion & Object Unloading: 

Objects that players aren't actively seeing will now be unloaded more efficiently, reducing unnecessary rendering.

Raycast Improvements: 

Various enhancements to how the game handles raycasts for better performance.

Optimization is a continuous process, we appreciate all the feedback we've received on this and you can be certain that we are going to continue improving it in the lead up to and throughout Early Access.

Quality of Life (QOL):

We saw a lot of feedback from players who found it challenging to understand certain elements of SAND, so we're putting an increased focus on improving the UI/UX for easier and more intuitive navigation while also working to make the trampler editor easier to understand and more accessible for players.  

We're also working on new systems to help newer players understand the goals of the game, how to play and what to do. This will act as a precursor to a full tutorial we have planned and hope to introduce further down the line.

In addition, we'll be making some refinements for the general in game user experience to ensure a more enjoyable, immersive and rewarding experience:


 Improving the shooting mechanics for better combat responsiveness.
 Players will be able to consume food to recover health
 Adding more details on the extraction process, ensuring that players are aware of what needs to be done to properly extract their loot safely.
 A ton of general balancing adjustments for mounted weapons and explosives
 Reworking the start of expeditions with an improved dropship sequence.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/449b8a587ba36291051fcff1b4279e5d78e379de.jpg

New Features:

We're also working away on implementing some popular community requests that we saw during recent playtests, which we hope to have at least early iterations of available upon the Early Access launch:

Progression Tree & Unlockable Compartments: Players will be able to unlock new compartments, opening up more customization and progression options.
Buried Treasure:  Keen eyed players will be able to locate and uncover buried loot in several locations around the map with the aid of a good old shovel
Crafting System: Crafting will play a larger role in gameplay, introducing more survival and resource management mechanics.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/d91f41f03435fc040f5221cabdfc5e88cbe31ea6.jpg

Beyond Early Access Launch:

Of course, this is just a fraction of what's going on behind the scenes and we have a ton more plans for how we plan to grow, improve and expand the game over the course of Early Access. Obviously we'll have a comprehensive roadmap on launch, but for a brief insight into some of our planned additions:


 More trampler compartments (crafting station, medical station, searchlight)
 New weapons and combat options (melee weapons, rocket launcher)
 Expanded crafting and industry systems
 New islands and biomes (desert anomalies, more diverse environments)
 Character improvements (customization, armor visualization, female characters)
 Enhanced multiplayer and communication systems (emotion-ping system, lobby system rework)
 Technical improvements (optimization, bug fixes, controller support, expanded localization)
 World and immersion upgrades (Sandstorms, companions system, achievements, expedition start cinematic)


Keep an eye out for the comprehensive roadmap closer to launch for more details on where we're planning on taking SAND!

[hr][/hr]

What's most important right now is that you're all aware that your feedback has been heard, and that we're doing everything we can to ensure that SAND not only meets, but exceeds all of your expectations on launch and beyond. And of course, we're extremely grateful for all of your feedback, support and participation in our betas these last few months.

notes.title: PLEASE READ: Fraudulent invites to SAND Playtest
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/61e4c4dd966b22f96dacb5151b6b40994efe251b.png

We’ve been made aware that some players may be receiving fraudulent invitations to a "SAND Playtest." 

Please note that no playtest is currently taking place, and we would never contact you via DM for participation or with an invite.

If you receive a message from someone claiming to offer access to a SAND playtest, do not click any links and report both the message and the sender immediately. These links are malicious and we are told can compromise your personal information and access to your accounts.

We have raised the issue with Valve and are working towards a solution.

For SAND updates, announcements, and playtest news, make sure to follow our official channels. Any active playtests will always be announced here in the steam announcements.

Thank you to everyone who brought this to our attention. Stay safe!

- Hologryph & tinyBuild Games

notes.title: SAND | November Development Update
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/f42ec25c1d429c3f087e15bdfe5d777a616494df.jpg

Hello Everybody,

With an intense few weeks now behind us, following the launch of the first SAND playtest that saw over 200,000 of you taking your first steps on Sophie, we wanted to give you all an update of how development on SAND is coming along and share some insights into what the team has been working on lately!

But before we get into it, we want to offer a huge thank you to all who participated, reported bugs, made suggestions and shared feedback. We are studying all of your propositions and ideas and adjusting our plans and priorities with them firmly in mind. 

It was a great experience for us and we are going to use all of your input to ensure an even better experience for you in SAND next time we invite you all back into the game! 

Optimization

First of all, we heard you, we know optimization needs to be addressed and performance improved and we are actively working on optimization to make your experience smoother. 

Our optimization process is currently deeply related to general visual improvements. And here's a look at our work-in-progress screen:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/61a8564cdcea6b71fc3743f0a3c2d689227958c2.png

Of course, we are working on other optimization methods alongside this, this was just the easiest to show off visually!

Servers and server stability

Secondly, in our pipeline a lot of server communication changes. So as some of you may be aware, our servers were inexplicably shut down, and therefore made the game totally inaccessible in the middle of the NEXT Fest. 

This was a huge disappointment for us and of course  our players and to prevent similar situations in the future we are planning to change our server provider before the next public playtest.

Requested Features

Prevention of spawn stalking We are planning on introducing trampler spawning spots - a safer space that will be harder to reach for those who are already on the surface.

Inventory management: We're adding more options to allow you to more freely manage your orbital storage including the splitting items during the expedition preparation.

Character deletion: There will be an option to delete characters.

New compartments and trampler customisation: We are planning to add various structural and functional trampler compartments including: stairs and closed turrets.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/66f7cbcc6ee4cfede6fd976d7314ca2973e6b2e1.jpg

Also, and obviously most importantly: A Trampler horn is on the way!

Bugfixes

We are working hard to address some of the more prominent or commonly reported bugs and issues, here's a list of some of our key focuses at this time:


 Bugged box in hands has been addressed.
 Tramplers will not get stuck in the air on spawn.
 The trampler will no longer get stuck on rocks or in the ground.
 A lot of character movement improvements.


Balance


 All compartments prices will be revised.
 Loot balance tweaks are underway.
 We are aware of various duping bugs and balance-breaking options, fixing all of them.
 Trampler movement and maneuverability balance will be revised. As a part of the new traveling experience we can give you a sneak peek of our new control panel:


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/1697445107bd3e8c861b270b0bf7d462f5ce598e.jpg

Anti-cheat

We want your experience to be as enjoyable, fair and honest as possible, so we are actively working on implementation of anti-cheat.

New weapons

Some new weapons are under development right now!

Here is a model of a new shotgun:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/6d4cf0680cb94d14ae5a8f94546e3070b9ade11c.jpg

What other weapons would you like to see come to the game?

Mines

Sneak peek of the naval mine field - a dangerous new zone on Sophie:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/0e1818f73b72823998b7a09670233638ab6f6a97.png

Explosive barrels

A lot of explosions ahead as these explosive barrels will soon arrive in the game as a new tactical feature. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/1775b7a717aecb19e3837eb2be97c7a306b9591d.png

Progression

One of the important points of our game design department is progression, and we have a few interesting features in mind regarding this which we're sure you're going to enjoy!

All we can reveal right now is that we are planning a gradual unlocking of trampler compartments. But we'll have more in-depth details on this stuff a little further down the line...

PvE

The most attentive of you already found some PvE on the Demo, more is of course planned, but we don't want to spoil anything just yet... ;)

And More!

Lots of features are under development to make your travel more interesting including island activities, desert activities, orbit changes, resource re-balance, items, and more!

Obviously, this is all a fraction of everything going on behind the scenes right now, but we wanted to make sure you were all aware that your feedback has been heard, and that we're committed to making SAND the best experience it can be, alongside all you wonderful folk who joined us for the first step of this journey.

Stay tuned for news on when you can next expect to visit Sophie again, and don't hesitate to share any feedback or suggestions in the comments!

Come and join us on our social media pages to keep yourself up to date with all the news and updates for SAND or join the discussion over on Discord now!

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/ec2cbb87f20facd499a65d27e82eb9c393a3e11b.jpg

SAND is taking part in the Steam Next Fest, and you can play the demo now!

In order to access the Demo, all you need to do is click "Install Demo" below, and it'll be added to your account!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3242130/SAND_Demo/

In this demo, the core gameplay is developed around building Tramplers and using them to explore the planet and fight against other players.

You can design, customize, and operate your personal Trampler, a walking mech that serves as both a mobile base and a combat vehicle. Use the Trampler editor to experiment with various weapons and upgrades, turning your Trampler into the ultimate base, method of exploration and battle machine. Experience PvP combat as you encounter other players in the open world, either solo or playing with your friends.

This demo offers just a glimpse of what SAND will become. The full game will be much more expansive, however for this test the goal is to ensure that the player vs player component works well before we continue to both develop existing mechanics and add new ones, such as NPCs, interactive points of interest, new compartments for Tramplers (both for PvP and PvE), new weapons, and different Metas to open new compartments.  

Check out some gameplay footage here:

[previewyoutube=abHXuNB-bks;full][/previewyoutube]

Please be aware:

The game is in the early stages of development, and the gameplay and mechanics in this build are not final. The primary goal of this demo is to test server load, PvP gameplay and give our players a bite of the SAND PvP experience.

There is currently no PvE content in this demo, but this will be present in the eventual release.
You may encounter bugs or performance issues, such as FPS drops. We are aware of these issues and are working to improve them, but please ensure your system meets the minimum recommended specs for the best experience.

notes.title: SAND Demo FAQ
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/df20a5a2d8d904c04db9cd930d7bddf7711e4c99.jpg

What is the SAND Demo?
In this demo, the core gameplay is developed around building Tramplers and using them to explore the planet and fight against other players.

This demo offers just a glimpse of what SAND will become. The full game will be much more expansive, however for this test the goal is to ensure that the player vs player component works well before we continue to both develop existing mechanics and add new ones, such as NPCs, interactive points of interest, new compartments for Tramplers (both for PvP and PvE), new weapons, and different Metas to open new compartments.

How can I play the demo?
You can download the demo on Steam page now 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3242130/SAND_Demo/

When will the full game be released?
We have not yet finalized a date for release, but as soon as this has been decided, we will announce it on all of the relevant channels.

What is the maximum size of a team?
Max size is 6, but for such a team you should have enough crew rooms on your trampler.

What are the minimum specs to play SAND?
CPU: Intel Corei7-9700, AMD Ryzen 5 3600
RAM: 24Gb
Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti, AMD Radeon RX 5700, Intel Arc A750

The name of the genre has "extraction". Does this mean that matches have a time limit?
No. Despite the fact that we taken a lot of cues from some of our favourite "extraction shooters", we do not limit players in how much time they can spend on the expedition on the surface. The players themselves decide when to finish and return to the extraction point to protect what they were able to find.

Is it be possible to ally with other crews?
Our design is based around ensuring that the game revolves around the struggles, successes and experiences of individual Crews, and not larger factions, which matchmaking will of course contribute towards. We are doing everything we can to ensure that the game does not devolve into battles of large groups/factions of regular players against beginners and solos.

Is it be possible to play solo?
Absolutely. We have designed and balanced the game specifically to ensure that players can enjoy it solo or alongside their friends.

Can I change the language of the game?
Only English is available for the tech demo but more languages will be added over time and upon launch.

Can I remap the key bindings?
While there is no such option in the demo at this time, key binding remapping will be available upon SANDs eventual launch.

How to split stacks on the plan expedition screen?
This system is not yet implemented in the Demo

What can I do if my trampler is stuck?
Try to move in all directions including strafe (Q/E).
Try to turn off and turn on your reactor.
If nothing helps - please create a topic in the Steam Bug Reports forum with the title "Trampler stuck".

What can I do if I lose all my resources?
If you have no tramplers and no resources to build new ones you will have to create a new character or join another team that owns a trampler to recover additional resources.

Can I delete my character?
Unfortunately, this is not possible at this time.
If you have no character slots and all your characters are broken, please create a thread on the bug report steam forum with the title "Wipe my characters".

I am experiencing some bugs and FPS drops, why?
You may encounter bugs or performance issues, such as FPS drops. We are aware of these issues and are working to improve them, but please ensure your system meets the minimum recommended specs for the best experience. Please also check our FAQ post in Steam Discussions for more information about settings that can be tweaked to improve performance.

Will the game be further optimized? 
Of course, this demo is a very early glimpse of the game and designed to test 3 key areas, PvP gameplay, Server stability and the trampler editor system, however as we continue to develop the game, will be focusing on optimization and ensuring smooth, stable gameplay.

How can I improve my FPS?

The ideal settings for the highest FPS at this time are as follows:

 Upscaler to FSR
 Upscaler set to Performance
 SSAO to Off
 SSGI to Off

The rest depends on your rig and can be tweaked accordingly:
Draw Distance
Shadow Quality
Texture Quality
Clouds Quality

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/2eb05fc92748a27b52828f76374c20ed8ba4d60b.png

Found a bug?
You can report this in the bug reporting subforum HERE

Have a request or proposition on how to make the game better?
You can either leave your suggestions HERE or you can  fill out the feedback form from the in-game link.
You will find the question "What content or feature would you most like to see in SAND?" at the end of the form.

notes.title: SAND Playtest Dates Update | Playtest Details
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/251404ac8a80594ae764c3f796d418e241f38f6b.png

Hello everyone. Maksym here, head of studio at Hologryph, to share some updates on the SAND playtest with you all. 

We’ll start things off with some news regarding dates:

We've been working hard and diligently on this build since spring, but in our efforts to make sure that you all had the best possible first experience with SAND, we found ourselves going much further in scope than we had planned and creating a lot more work for ourselves than we had initially prepared for. As a result, the playtest build will be much larger in scope than anticipated but we will be slightly delaying the playtest beyond summer to early in the 4th quarter of 2024. 

However, to tide you over in the meantime, we've released a Devlog giving you an exclusive first look at the new trampler editor, featuring some new gameplay footage 👇

[previewyoutube=-vTQROS7sEU;full][/previewyoutube]

For an additional little bit of good news: Almost everything has come together. In its current state, the game is playable, fun and a good representation of our vision and direction for the game. If it weren't for the risk of losing hours of progress due to bugs, we would already be inviting players, but we are working on that now and confident that we will have it fixed soon.

Now for some information about the playtest itself

For the Playtest, we've prepared a build that focuses primarily on PvP, removing the planned PvE elements for the time being. We need your help to ensure that player combat works properly, to find and fix all the bugs, and to take your feedback into account before we use that feedback to integrate alongside the PvE aspects of SAND.

Playtest details:

 You can team up with friends on Steam.
 Server worlds are fully procedurally generated (with pre-made POI’s randomly spawned throughout)
 We have introduced a full, robust Trampler Editor where you can completely customize the layout, equipment, storage, size, maneuverability and fortification of your vessel.  
 The Trampler Editor is fully functional, allowing the captain to build and choose a Trampler for the expedition.
 You can also choose a pre-made trampler for your expeditions
 On the moon, you can gather resources and search for equipment to complete contracts (missions/tasks) for even more valuable rewards.
 Some resources are only accessible through contracts that can be found on the map.
 All of this is on a server with a dozen other teams.
 Once you feel like you've had enough, head to the extraction point and try to secure the resources you've gathered.
 Upon reaching orbit, you can modify your Trampler with use of the resources extracted and your battle experience.
 Then, embark on a new expedition.


As soon as we achieve and are confident in our client and server stability, we will announce the Playtest dates. Initially, we will invite a limited number of people, and once we’ve got the initial growing pains and prevalent issues resolved, we will open access to everyone who has applied.

Thank you for your understanding, we can’t wait to see you in the realms of Sofia!

notes.title: SAND Dev Diary #2 | The World of SAND
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/dc0d463c5b4dba59f6c5f518ebaf4a5254f19f72.jpg

 Welcome back to the second in our series of SAND Dev Diaries!

Today, we're diving into the world of SAND as we detail the pivotal events that shaped this universe, reveal the circumstances that led to the colonization of the moon Sophie, unveil exactly why our characters are so eager to return to this unforgiving moon and more... 

Read on to find out more

[hr][/hr]

The Story of Sand:

The Austro-Hungarian Empire, known for its multiculturalism and traditions, discovered a new energy source in the 19th century. Accelerated technical progress led to the creation of a space portal to the Ursae Majoris star system. High construction costs led to the empire seeking alliances with other empires, which, in a tale as old as time, also led to territorial divisions and quarrels based on investment. Ultimately, Austria-Hungary colonized the planets which they later named Franz, Rudolf, and the satellite moons of the gas giant (having invested the most money into the project at the time), while allies like Great Britain, USA and Germany settled upon more distant regions.

To appease growing demands for rights and space territory, the Emperor instructed his heir (Franz Ferdinand) to develop a project of a new system for space colonies. The project was named “the United Star States of Great Austria”, dividing planets among different national groups. As a result, the satellite moon “Sophie” was allocated to Eastern and Western Galicia. However, before the colonization project had been completed, an ecological disaster rendered Sophie almost uninhabitable, whereby the Kaiser abandoned further funding for its restoration, and froze the project. 

However, the Galicians, driven by promises of land, persist in claiming what was once offered to them to this day...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/ac2035ca756ced762ca9f56d3f0382a55284dabb.jpg

The Setting:

Sophie, a satellite moon intended to become a paradise rich in resources and resorts, was the subject of a catastrophic disaster 30 years into its colonization, where a mysterious, and still as yet unexplained cataclysm turned its oceans into vast deserts of sand, wiping out swathes of the population and all but destroying any hope of the prosperous future that had been promised to its colonizers. The authorities managed to evacuate much of the existing population, but in doing so were forced to abandon most of their equipment and property. 

Massive sandstorms and scorching heat made the moon almost uninhabitable for 20 years, leaving Sophie a desolate, desert expanse and its formerly bustling cities as ghost towns, filled with valuable items and resources that lay as remnants of the life that once was.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/253c0222dc18ca1b9e4f13bb12ceb4ece3a3f9bb.jpg

Tramplers:

Tramplers, large ship-like vehicles with movable chassis, were initially used to transport construction materials during Sophie’s colonization. Designed to move both on land and water, they became invaluable post-disaster. Operated mainly by laborers from poorer regions, tramplers have evolved over time into highly customized machines. The ability to modify them for specific tasks, improving their capabilities, size, durability and more with available modular enhancements making them the perfect vehicle for enduring the many dangers posed on Sophie. 

Battles involving tramplers are highly strategic, and in order to succeed, a strong focus must be put on destroying or disabling integral parts of an enemy's vehicle. The player's understanding of their trampler's mechanics significantly impacts their combat effectiveness, making the bond between player and machine crucial.

https://i.imgur.com/kuomN3W.gif

The Characters:

Players assume the roles of Galicians, primarily Ukrainians from a region of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Promised land on Sophie by the Kaiser, they initially volunteered as laborers for its colonization. Despite the disaster, their dream of owning space land and living in luxury endured, a fact that was not overlooked by a Viennese Space Travel Agency who illegal deployed recruitment agents to the impoverished regions in order to spread word of the prospect of quick riches for those who dared return to the desolate moon that was once promised to them.

Due to the high cost of space travel, these illegal schemes require travelers to give a portion of their loot to the agents to cover ticket costs, with each space station having an "authorized" individual who issues return tickets only after debts are paid on the spot.

https://i.imgur.com/D2zQU2b.gif

[hr][/hr]

Thanks for reading! Let us know which aspects of the game you'd like to hear more about in the comments thread and we'll see if we can fit it in for a future Dev Diary!

notes.title: SAND Dev Diary #1 | An Introduction To SAND
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238322/8f9b645b9800663783d402cfbf0ad86f0f5ddbf1.png

Welcome to the first of our new Dev Diaries series! 

Over the next few weeks, we'll join members of our development team to provide you with an exclusive peek into the world of SAND, delving into its development journey, future plans, world, art and upcoming content as we progress towards future playtests and the game's eventual release!

In this initial Q&A, Development Lead Maksym will introduce the fundamentals of SAND and address some of the most pressing questions from our community about the strange and hostile world players will soon find themselves fighting for survival in.

So let's get to it... 

[hr][/hr]

What Exactly is SAND?

SAND is an open-world multiplayer extraction shooter where players explore the vast, fallen satellite moon named Sophie, with the aid of gigantic walking mechs known as Tramplers.

The game is set during the colonization of space by the Austro-Hungarian Empire on the eve of the First World War. Players will find themselves in the middle of the deserts on an unknown planet, beginning their journey in search of resources and valuables. To aid in their journeys, players can design and modify their personal Trampler – a machine essential for efficiently navigating the vast desert plains and surviving encounters with enemy factions.

https://i.imgur.com/sjGQuRH.gif

Tell me more about the history of this moon “Sophie”?

Sophie is a satellite moon on which the Austro-Hungarian Empire had hoped to build a colony, granting land to Ukrainians and Poles from the Galician region. Initially, the colony thrived, with cities and factories being constructed and a growing population flocking to the moon in hopes of a prosperous future. 

However, a mysterious catastrophe occurred, which resulted in an urgent evacuation (the details of which players can uncover) before eventually the Kaiser ordered the moon's complete closure. 
Over time, as Sophie began to “heal”, adventurers and scavengers returned, driven by the belief that treasures and valuables left behind during the evacuation could offer them a chance at a luxurious life which the Empire could no longer provide. 

https://i.imgur.com/VbEhXxN.gif

What makes the game stand out from other similar titles?

The central feature of SAND is the Tramplers, which allow players to explore the remnants of the Austro-Hungarian Empire's luxury in the post-apocalyptic world of Sophie. Not only used for traversal however, equipping your trampler with weapons and fortifications is essential, as players will have to survive encounters with opposing players/their tramplers and an array of creatures that roam the planet that are more than capable of dismantling an ill equipped team.

Additionally, SAND's approach to alternative history is something we haven't seen replicated in any similar titles. The game balances real events with imaginative twists, exploring intriguing historical possibilities that were hindered by events such as the deaths of key historical politicians or scientists.

https://i.imgur.com/aAyk0CI.gif

What kind of challenges and dangers can we expect in this world?

After the mysterious catastrophe, Sophie became an extremely hostile environment. Players will face the challenge of surviving the scorching daytime heat and the bitter cold that sweeps the planet after sunset, endless deserts and sandstorms while battling native inhabitants that somehow survived the ecosystem's collapse. More hazards are planned in the form of additional NPCs, weather events and more, but we’ll talk more about them at a later date.

https://i.imgur.com/YBppKne.gif

What is the Goal of the Game?

The primary goal of SAND is to explore the world, survive engagements with competing scavengers, locate valuable items left behind after the disaster, extract them, and sell them to fund future expeditions and improvements for your tramplers and starting equipment. 

Make yourself rich, make yourself powerful, make yourself famous

Obviously, everything and everyone in the world will be doing what they can to obstruct you in this mission and achieve their own goals, so keep your wits about you...

https://i.imgur.com/A0kfwDQ.gif

[hr][/hr]

Thanks for reading! Let us know which aspects of the game you'd like to hear more about in the comments thread and we'll see if we can wrangle some information out of the devs for a future Dev Diary!

This summer, we invite you all to join us in the first beta for SAND, which you can sign up to participate in now on the Steam page 👇
